recommendations.regimenLabel: Permissive hypotension + major haemorrhage protocol, then emergency repair
steps: EMERGENCY — call vascular surgery immediately; do NOT delay for extensive imaging if unstable.
Permissive hypotension (avoid aggressive fluids/overshoot before repair); large-bore access, major haemorrhage protocol.
Immediate transfer to theatre / endovascular suite for repair (EVAR or open).
CT angiography only if stable enough.

drugRefs.dose: transfuse via major haemorrhage protocol, targeting permissive hypotension
drugRefs.freq: titrated to perfusion until surgical control
drugRefs.why: Ruptured AAA is haemorrhagic shock; balanced blood-product resuscitation (with FFP/platelets per protocol) restores oxygen delivery while awaiting definitive repair. Definitive treatment is surgical, not pharmacological.

drugRefs.dose: minimise volume; target SBP ~70–90 mmHg (or palpable radial pulse / preserved consciousness) until repair
drugRefs.why: Aggressive fluid loading raises BP and dislodges clot, worsening bleeding; keep pressure low until surgical control.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Diseases of the Aorta
ESVS 2019 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-iliac Artery Aneurysms

confirm: Sudden abdominal/back/flank pain with hypotension and a pulsatile mass in an older patient — ruptured AAA until proven otherwise.

investigations.test: Bedside US / CT angio if stable
